items.title: Sky Television launches
items.line: Sky began broadcasting on 5 February 1989 with four channels on the Astra 1A satellite. It merged with rival BSB on 2 November 1990.

items.title: The web proposal
items.line: In March 1989 Tim Berners-Lee handed CERN a proposal for an information system with no name yet. By the end of 1990 the first browser and server were running.

items.title: Hillsborough
items.line: 97 Liverpool supporters died after a crush at the FA Cup semi-final against Nottingham Forest at Hillsborough, Sheffield, on 15 April 1989.

items.title: Game Boy
items.line: Nintendo's Game Boy came out in Japan on 21 April 1989 and North America on 31 July, with Tetris in the box outside Japan. Europe waited until September 1990.

items.title: Batman
items.line: Tim Burton's Batman was shot at Pinewood and opened in the US on 23 June 1989 and the UK on 11 August. It cost $48 million and took $411.6 million.

items.title: The Berlin Wall opens
items.line: At about 18:53 on 9 November 1989 Günter Schabowski told a press conference the new travel rules took effect immediately, and that night Berliners crossed.
